headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: B can write and run subprocesses while A is non-runnable and read-only, but shared-channel risks are otherwise limited by A's lack of I/O surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no I/O surfaces or runnable behavior, so direct injection into A is not evidenced. B does read/write files and uses shared skill files, so if operators manually copy A-derived content into B’s workspace, prompt-like contamination is possible. This is a limited, manual bridge rather than a default channel.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into B-managed skill files or prompts, injection risk appears.
IF B is configured to ingest shared markdown or skill files as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of B prompt files.
Review any copied markdown before placing it in .agents/ or .claude/ paths.
Use a separate scratch directory for A-derived artifacts.
Add a manual approval step before B consumes external text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network surfaces, while B can read/write files and call allowlisted APIs. There is no documented shared workspace or sensitive data class overlap, so leakage is not established by default. The main risk is operator-mediated copying into B’s files.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in B’s readable workspace, B can ingest them.
IF operators copy private content from A into B’s skill files, that content may flow to allowlisted APIs.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in B’s workspace.
Restrict B’s API calls to non-sensitive projects.
Use separate directories for A and B artifacts.
Delete copied drafts after review.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has write_filesystem, read_filesystem, and spawn_subprocesses; A is non-runnable and exposes no write surface. There is no direct overlap with A, but B’s own mutable workspace and multiple instances create conflict potential if A-derived artifacts are manually introduced into the same directory. Uncertainty is limited, but the pair is not conflict-free.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, B can overwrite A-derived artifacts.
IF multiple B instances operate on the same files, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent B instances on shared files.
Use file locks for any shared artifact.
Keep A outputs read-only.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s sandboxing says skills reference each other and build on shared context, which makes it plausible that B treats upstream text as authoritative. A is a course/repo with no runnable output, so the cascade is indirect rather than automatic. Still, if A-derived content is imported into B’s shared context, B may propagate errors without verification.
conditions: IF A-derived text is inserted into B’s shared context, B may reuse it as authoritative.
IF B is tasked to generate deliverables from imported notes, errors can cascade into outputs.
mitigations: Verify imported facts before reuse.
Mark A-derived text as untrusted.
Require source links in B outputs.
Separate draft and final folders.
requires-engineering: add citation validation.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source data-engineering course with no touched data classes, while B handles marketing content and product marketing context. No residency, retention, or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary content handling. The other agent is not cited for a specific violation because none is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into B’s marketing workspace, compliance obligations change.
IF A is repurposed to process personal data, its current documentation no longer applies.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document data-class boundaries.
Review retention settings for B’s files.
Use separate repositories for course and marketing content.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
